chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The sons are a bounties (or delight), and the daughters are good deeds (or blessings), and Allah will ask about the bounties and will reward for the good deeds.

key_terms.نَعِيمٌ: Bounties or delight (often implying something to be enjoyed but also accounted for)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the spiritual status of sons and daughters in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the unique spiritual merit of daughters, distinguishing them as 'hasanat' (good deeds) rather than mere 'ne'im' (bounties/trials). This distinction implies that while sons are a test requiring accountability, daughters are a direct reward for which parents receive divine recompense, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition regarding family dynamics. The hadith underscores the elevated status of daughters in Islamic spirituality, framing their upbringing as an act of worship that yields immediate spiritual dividends.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Musa, from Ahmad Bin Al Fazl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The sons are Bounties, and the daughters are blessings, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Question about the Bounties but He<sup>azwj</sup> would Rewards upon the ‘حَسَنَاتٌ’ (blessings).
en.sarwar: 12. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Musa from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Sons are bounties and daughters are good deeds, Allah questions one about the bounties but for the good deeds He gives good rewards.”’
